grades.quote: Thus, even if there is a multilevel page table behind the scenes, it will be used only rarely.
grades.reason: Discusses how a linear page table is combined with a multilevel page table and how the TLB affects lookups. It does not explain how a multilevel table saves space for sparse address spaces. It only mentions the multilevel table as a backing structure.

grades.quote: You can store those chunks of the page table that contain any valid entries, even if there are also a few invalid entries mixed in, and not store those chunks that contain entirely invalid entries.
grades.reason: Explains the core idea behind the space savings. Address-space use is clumped and sparse, so the page table can be stored in page-sized chunks. Chunks with no valid entries need no frames. It frames this around a linear page table kept in virtual memory and only points to multilevel page tables, so it is not a direct multilevel explanation.
Covers xv6 RISC-V trap handling from user space (trampoline, uservec, sscratch). It says nothing about multilevel page tables or sparse address-space savings.

grades.quote: Whether the LDDIR and LDPTE instructions are used to implement software page walking or hardware page walking, the supported multi-level page table structure is the same, as shown in the figure.
grades.reason: Describes the LoongArch multi-level page table structure (directory levels, PGD selection, entry formats). It does not explain how this saves space when large virtual ranges are unused.
